recentItems.title: Bronx News Today: Metro-North bomb hoax case and Bronx officer shooting
recentItems.description:
An off-duty NYPD officer identified by family as 33-year-old Demitrious Caceres accidentally shot himself in the leg at a Bailey Avenue home in Kingsbridge Heights, prompting an investigation. Also in this Bronx-area roundup, Albertina Mendoza was indicted for allegedly making false bomb threat reports involving a Metro-North train, FDNY crews battled a fire on Crotona Avenue, police searched for four suspects accused of robbing a man in Norwood, authorities confirmed missing 87-year-old Josefina Perez has been found, and officials celebrated the opening of a new affordable and supportive housing development for seniors on Tiebout Avenue.

recentItems.title: Fake Trump Presidential Limo pulled over, impounded in the Hamptons
recentItems.description:
A replica of President Trump's limousine, known as "The Beast," was impounded by Southampton Village Police after investigators say it was using unauthorized blue and red lights. Police say they found a fake shotgun, a New York license plate, six fake Washington, D.C., license plates, and other items inside the vehicle. The car's owner, the founder of the Setaucket Patriots, says the vehicle is used for car shows and contains display props. Police issued summonses, and the Secret Service has been notified and is investigating.

recentItems.title: Body found inside burned-out car after explosion rocks Bridgeport neighborhood
recentItems.description:

Police say a body was discovered inside the burned-out car and investigators have remained on scene collecting evidence. Residents described the incident as upsetting and scary as authorities work to determine what happened.

recentItems.description:

Lawmakers are also raising concerns about inspector staffing levels and violations found at cooling towers that tested positive for the bacteria.

recentItems.description:

recentItems.title: Baby killed in crash during unlicensed driver’s lesson in NJ
recentItems.description:
New details revealed in court shed light on the deadly Jackson Township crash that killed a 9-month-old baby and seriously injured the child’s mother and 5-year-old sister. Prosecutors say Maria Cobon Guzman, an unlicensed driver was behind the wheel during a driving lesson when the crash happened, and allege a friend, Ariadna Lazaro-Flores handed over the keys. A judge ordered both women held in jail pending trial. According to ICE, both women are in the United States illegally. ICE filed detainers on both defendants.
